newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police raid troubled state nuclear firm.
newsitem.headline: Japan police raid troubled state nuclear firm.

text.p: Police raided a troubled state-run nuclear firm on Wednesday looking for evidence to support a criminal complaint over its false reporting of Japan's worst-ever nuclear accident last month.

A spokesman for the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp said officers raided both the firm's Tokyo headquarters and its nuclear fuel reprocessing plant in Tokaimura on the Pacific coast, the scene of the accident.

The raids followed a criminal complaint by government's Science and Technology Agency, which founded PNC and oversees its operations. Police searched the offices of senior executives of the firm, the PNC spokesman said.

The Science and Technology Agency filed a criminal complaint against PNC after the firm admitted early this month it had falsified a report relating to an explosion at Tokaimura on March 11 that exposed 37 workers to low levels of radiation.
The complaint charges that in filing the report PNC violated laws governing the operation of nuclear reactors.

PNC said it incorrectly stated in the report that staff had visually confirmed that a fire at a nuclear waste facility had been extinguished. No staff members had confirmed this and the fire later flared up, triggering the explosion. It was Japan's worst nuclear accident.

Just before the Science and Technology Agency filed its complaint, it ordered PNC to shut down its "Fugen" advanced thermal reactor in western Japan after the firm admitted it had waited 30 hours before reporting a radiation leak that exposed 11 workers to low-levels of radiation.

The PNC subsequently acknowledged that it had not reported 18 separate radiation leaks at the 18-year-old reactor since 1992, maintaining that the amount of leaked radiation was below the level at which it was legally required to do so.
On Tuesday, the head of PNC apologised for the errors and told parliament the firm was discussing privatising its two main functions.

PNC President Toshiyuki Kondo said the firm was in talks on turning its uranium enrichment and nuclear fuel reprocessing operations over to the private sector, But he said the PNC would still play a major role in Japan's nuclear programme.

"No private-sector body is capable of taking over the development of fast-breeder reactors, the recycling of fuel, or the disposal of high-level radioactive waste," Kondo told a parliamentary committee.

The PNC is at the heart of Japan's ambitions to boost electricity output from nuclear plants to 42 percent of total power needs by 2010. Nuclear plants now supply one-third of Japan's total power output.
To mend fences with the Tokaimura plant's neighbours, PNC officials spent this week making house-to-house visits to apologise for last month's accident and the false report.
